Apis mellifera.habitat: Meadows, gardens, agricultural areas, and open woodlands.
Apis mellifera.general_behavior: Generally docile and non-aggressive unless their hive is threatened or they are physically stepped on/handled.
Apis mellifera.fun_fact: Honey bees communicate the distance, direction, and quality of food sources by performing a specialized 'waggle dance'.

Crotalus oreganus.habitat: Arid deserts, rocky hillsides, scrublands, and dry pine forests.
Crotalus oreganus.general_behavior: Shy and prefers to retreat, but will rattle loudly as a warning and strike defensively if cornered, startled, or stepped on.
Crotalus oreganus.fun_fact: A rattlesnake's rattle is made of hollow interlocking segments of keratin, which is the same material as human fingernails.

Trimeresurus sabahi fucatus.habitat: Tropical wet rainforests, bamboo thickets, and low shrubs in mountainous areas.
Trimeresurus sabahi fucatus.general_behavior: Arboreal hunter that spends daytime coiled in low branches. Highly venomous and strikes quickly if approached too closely.
Trimeresurus sabahi fucatus.fun_fact: Pit vipers possess heat-sensitive pits between their eyes and nostrils that allow them to 'see' the thermal signature of warm-blooded prey in pitch blackness.

Latrodectus mactans.habitat: Dark, sheltered areas such as woodpiles, stone walls, barns, garages, and basements.
Latrodectus mactans.general_behavior: Extremely reclusive and non-aggressive. They spend their time hanging upside down in webs and bite humans only in self-defense when squeezed.
Latrodectus mactans.fun_fact: Female black widows are famously known for occasionally consuming the male spider after mating, giving them their name.

Ursus arctos horribilis.habitat: Temperate forests, alpine meadows, river valleys, and tundra.
Ursus arctos horribilis.general_behavior: Solitary and territorial. They are highly protective of their cubs and food sources and may charge if startled at close range.
Ursus arctos horribilis.fun_fact: Despite their massive weight of up to 800 pounds, grizzly bears can sprint at speeds reaching 35 miles per hour.
